title: E-Commerce Checkout Automation Suite
summary: End-to-end Playwright automation framework covering the full checkout journey across 3 payment gateways.
overview: The client's checkout flow spanned guest checkout, saved cards, wallets and 3 payment gateways. Manual regression before every release took 2 full QA days and still missed edge cases in coupon stacking and currency conversion.
approach: Built a Page Object Model framework in Playwright + TypeScript with fixtures for auth, cart seeding and mock payment responses.
Designed a data-driven test matrix covering 45 checkout scenarios across currencies, coupons and payment methods.
Wired the suite into GitHub Actions with parallel sharding (6 workers) and Allure HTML reporting on every PR.
Added visual regression checks on the payment summary screen using Playwright's screenshot assertions.
findings: Found a race condition where double-clicking 'Place Order' created duplicate charges under slow network throttling.
Caught a currency rounding bug that under-charged EUR customers by up to 0.02 per order.
Identified that coupon stacking silently failed when two percentage-based coupons were applied together.

title: REST API Contract & Load Testing Framework
summary: API test suite with schema validation, contract testing and load benchmarks for a fintech microservices backend.
overview: A fintech client's 14 microservices had no contract tests, causing breaking changes to slip into staging repeatedly. Needed a suite that could run in under 5 minutes as part of the deploy pipeline.
approach: Authored 200+ Postman/Newman collections with JSON schema validation for every response.
Introduced contract tests using Pact between the payments and ledger services.
Built a lightweight load test harness with k6 to benchmark p95 latency under 500 concurrent users.
Integrated Newman + k6 runs into GitLab CI with Slack alerts on failure.
findings: Discovered the ledger service silently dropped the 'idempotency-key' header, risking duplicate transactions.
Found p95 latency spiked to 3.2s under load on the balance endpoint due to a missing DB index.
Caught 3 breaking schema changes before they reached staging in the first month alone.

title: CI/CD Quality Gates for Multi-Team Monorepo
summary: Designed automated quality gates (lint, unit, E2E, coverage thresholds) for a 30-engineer monorepo.
overview: With 30 engineers pushing to a single monorepo, release quality was inconsistent — some PRs merged with failing tests silently ignored. The team needed enforced quality gates without slowing everyone down.
approach: Set up Jenkins multibranch pipelines with staged gates: lint → unit → integration → E2E smoke.
Configured branch protection so merges require green E2E smoke suite (Playwright) on a preview environment.
Introduced coverage thresholds (80% lines) enforced via Jest with a merge-blocking check.
Built a dashboard (Grafana) tracking flaky test rate and pipeline duration over time.
findings: Identified 14 flaky tests responsible for 60% of false-positive pipeline failures; stabilized with proper waits.
Reduced average PR pipeline time from 22 minutes to 9 minutes via parallelization and caching.
Prevented 5 production incidents in the first quarter by blocking merges on failing smoke tests.

title: Automated Excel Test Reporting Dashboard
summary: A VBA + Python powered reporting pipeline that turns raw test run logs into stakeholder-ready Excel dashboards.
overview: Stakeholders wanted a readable weekly QA status report, but the team was manually copy-pasting test results into Excel every Friday — taking 3+ hours and prone to errors.
approach: Wrote a Python script to parse JUnit/Allure XML output and normalize results into a structured dataset.
Built an Excel template with pivot tables, conditional formatting and a pass/fail trend chart, auto-refreshed via openpyxl.
Automated the whole pipeline with a scheduled task that emails the report every Friday at 5 PM.
Added a 'QA status convention' color legend (Green/Amber/Red) tied to defect severity and pass rate thresholds.
findings: Eliminated 3+ hours of manual reporting work per week for the QA team.
Surfaced a recurring module (claims-upload) with a consistently declining pass rate, prompting a focused test sprint.
Standardized how 'release readiness' was communicated to non-technical stakeholders.
